rows.response_text:
Based on the given passages, here's a possible answer to the question "How to make a clay boat buoyant":

To make a clay boat buoyant, you need to shape it into a form that can displace enough water to compensate for its mass, just like a real boat. Start by flattening the clay into an even, rectangular flat sheet. The thinner it is, the more buoyant your boat will be. Then, fold the ends of the boat together to make an enclosed box. Pinch the ends together to get a tight seal. This will create a boat that can float on water due to the buoyant force, which is equal to the weight of the water the boat displaces.

However, it's important to note that the clay boat may not be able to support itself in the water without additional support, as it may not displace enough water to counteract its own weight. In this case, you can try adding weights to the boat or using a different material that is less dense than water.

Make sure your tray is once again dry and your bowl is filled up to the brim with water. 2  Have your child place the clay in the water and observe together how much water now drips onto the tray (it should be more this time).
